# pbs_sync_job (Resource)

Manages a Proxmox Backup Server sync job: on a schedule, it copies the backups of one datastore, or of a namespace in it, to another, skipping those the target has already. One resource covers three kinds of job:

* **pull from a remote** — `remote` set, `sync_direction = "pull"`, the default: from `remote_store` on the remote to `store` here;
* **local pull** — `remote` left out: from `remote_store`, another datastore of this server, to `store`;
* **push** — `sync_direction = "push"`, which needs `remote`: from `store` here to `remote_store` on the remote.

An offsite copy is either a push job on the PBS that holds the backups, or a pull job on the offsite one: a pull keeps the offsite server's credentials off the primary server, a push the primary's off the offsite one.

PBS checks neither the datastores nor the remote when it saves the job; a wrong name shows when the job runs.

Deleting a datastore without `keep_job_configs` deletes the sync jobs whose `store` it is — pulls always, pushes from PBS 4.1.1, while older releases keep a push job whose source is gone — and a `pbs_sync_job` then plans to create its job again. A local pull from the datastore is kept.

**Privileges.** The user or token the provider signs in as needs, besides `Datastore.Audit` on `/datastore/<store>[/<ns>]` to read the job:

* to pull from a remote, `Datastore.Backup` there — plus `Datastore.Prune` for `remove_vanished`, and `Datastore.Modify` unless `owner` is exactly the user or token the provider signs in as, or a token of that user — and `Remote.Read` on `/remote/<remote>/<remote_store>`; reading the job also needs `Remote.Audit` on `/remote/<remote>`;
* for a local pull, the same on `store`, and on `/datastore/<remote_store>[/<remote_ns>]` `Datastore.Audit` with `Datastore.Read`, or `Datastore.Backup` for the owner's own backups;
* to push, `RemoteDatastore.Backup` on `/remote/<remote>/<remote_store>[/<remote_ns>]` — plus `RemoteDatastore.Prune` for `remove_vanished` — and `Datastore.Read` on `/datastore/<store>[/<ns>]`, or `Datastore.Backup`, with `Datastore.Modify` unless `owner` is the provider's own, for the owner's own backups; reading the job also needs `Remote.Audit` on the remote path.

With an `owner` other than root@pam, the owner itself needs the same privileges on this server when the job runs. On the remote, `auth_id` of the `pbs_remote` acts: to pull, it needs `Datastore.Audit` with `Datastore.Read` on the remote datastore — the role `DatastoreReader` — or `Datastore.Backup` for its own backups; to push, `Datastore.Backup` there, plus `Datastore.Prune` for `remove_vanished` and `Datastore.Modify` to create the namespaces it pushes into.

The resource leaves the sync encryption keys of PBS 4.2, `active-encryption-key` and `associated-key`, alone: a job keeps the ones set in the web interface.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Every night, push the backups of pbs_datastore.store1, of the pbs_datastore
# example, to the datastore offsite1 of pbs_remote.offsite, of the pbs_remote
# example, both assumed in the same configuration. Only backups the offsite
# copy lacks are sent, at most 50 MB per second. Retention offsite is the
# offsite server's own: a prune job there.
resource "pbs_sync_job" "offsite" {
  id             = "push-offsite"
  sync_direction = "push"
  store          = pbs_datastore.store1.name
  remote         = pbs_remote.offsite.name
  remote_store   = "offsite1"
  schedule       = "21:00"
  rate_out       = "50MB"
  comment        = "Offsite copy of cluster1's backups"
}

# Pull, the default direction, copies the other way: here, every Saturday,
# the backups of VMs in the offsite server's datastore archive, but for those
# of VM 100, into the namespace archive of store1, which the job creates. The
# remote's auth_id needs to read the archive datastore there, with the role
# DatastoreReader, say.
resource "pbs_sync_job" "archive" {
  id           = "pull-archive"
  store        = pbs_datastore.store1.name
  ns           = "archive"
  remote       = pbs_remote.offsite.name
  remote_store = "archive"
  schedule     = "sat 04:00"
  group_filter = ["type:vm", "exclude:group:vm/100"]
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) Job ID, 3 to 32 characters: letters, digits, `_`, `.` and `-`, not starting with `.` or `-`. Changing it replaces the job.
- `remote_store` (String) Datastore on the remote — the source of a pull, the target of a push — or, without `remote`, the local datastore to pull from, which must be another than `store`.
- `store` (String) Local datastore, such as the `name` of a `pbs_datastore`: the target of a pull, the source of a push.

### Optional

- `burst_in` (String) How many bytes over `rate_in` the job may receive at once. A byte size such as `500`, `64KiB`, `10MiB` or `1.5GB`: `K`, `M`, `G`, `T` and `P` are powers of 1000, `Ki` to `Pi` powers of 1024, and `B` is optional. PBS writes it back in its own spelling, such as `10 MiB`, which counts as the same: state keeps the configuration's. Only after an import, state has PBS's spelling, and the next plan shows an update that sends nothing. No limit when left out.
- `burst_out` (String) How many bytes over `rate_out` the job may send at once. A byte size such as `500`, `64KiB`, `10MiB` or `1.5GB`: `K`, `M`, `G`, `T` and `P` are powers of 1000, `Ki` to `Pi` powers of 1024, and `B` is optional. PBS writes it back in its own spelling, such as `10 MiB`, which counts as the same: state keeps the configuration's. Only after an import, state has PBS's spelling, and the next plan shows an update that sends nothing. No limit when left out.
- `comment` (String) Free-form comment, up to 128 characters on one line.
- `encrypted_only` (Boolean) Whether to copy only encrypted backups. Defaults to `false`.
- `group_filter` (Set of String) Which backup groups to sync, all of them when left out. Each filter is `type:<vm|ct|host>`, `group:<type>/<id>` such as `group:vm/100`, or `regex:<expression>`, which is matched against `<type>/<id>` anywhere in it; `exclude:` in front of a filter excludes what it matches. A group is synced when it matches at least one filter that is not an exclude — or there is none — and no exclude.
- `max_depth` (Number) How many levels of namespaces below the source namespace to sync too, from `0`, the namespace alone, to `7`; all of them when left out. Added to the depth of `ns` and of `remote_ns`, it must not exceed 7, the deepest that namespaces nest.
- `ns` (String) Namespace in `store`, such as `dept1` or `dept1/hosts`; the datastore's root namespace when left out. A pull creates the namespaces it copies below it; a push copies from it, and it must exist.
- `owner` (String) User or API token of this server that the job acts as, such as `sync@pbs`; `root@pam` when left out. A pull makes it the owner of the backup groups it creates, and fails to sync a group the target has with another owner, so that the run ends with errors; a push copies the backups it may read. Leaving it out, or naming another user or token than the one the provider signs in as, needs `Datastore.Modify` on the target of a pull, and on the source of a push unless the provider has `Datastore.Read` there; `root@pam` needs neither. When the job runs, the owner needs the job's privileges on this server: a pull creates the namespaces it copies as the owner, which needs `Datastore.Modify` on their parent.
- `rate_in` (String) Rate limit on the data the job receives from the remote, the copies of a pull, in bytes per second. A byte size such as `500`, `64KiB`, `10MiB` or `1.5GB`: `K`, `M`, `G`, `T` and `P` are powers of 1000, `Ki` to `Pi` powers of 1024, and `B` is optional. PBS writes it back in its own spelling, such as `10 MiB`, which counts as the same: state keeps the configuration's. Only after an import, state has PBS's spelling, and the next plan shows an update that sends nothing. No limit when left out.
- `rate_out` (String) Rate limit on the data the job sends to the remote, the copies of a push, in bytes per second. A byte size such as `500`, `64KiB`, `10MiB` or `1.5GB`: `K`, `M`, `G`, `T` and `P` are powers of 1000, `Ki` to `Pi` powers of 1024, and `B` is optional. PBS writes it back in its own spelling, such as `10 MiB`, which counts as the same: state keeps the configuration's. Only after an import, state has PBS's spelling, and the next plan shows an update that sends nothing. No limit when left out.
- `remote` (String) Name of the other PBS, such as the `name` of a `pbs_remote`. Required to push; when left out, the job pulls from a datastore of this server.
- `remote_ns` (String) Namespace in `remote_store`, such as `site-a`; its root namespace when left out. A push creates the namespaces it copies below it on the remote.
- `remove_vanished` (Boolean) Whether to delete, from the target, the backups, backup groups and namespaces the source no longer has, protected backups excepted. Defaults to `false`. A vanished backup group is deleted only when `group_filter` selects it and the job owns it — for a pull, `owner`; for a push, the remote's `auth_id` — but a vanished namespace below `ns` (pull) or `remote_ns` (push) is deleted with every backup group in it, whatever the filter and owners. With `encrypted_only` or `verified_only`, backups the source has but the filter skips count as gone.
- `resync_corrupt` (Boolean) Whether a pull copies again the backups whose local copy failed verification. Defaults to `false`. Pull jobs only.
- `run_on_mount` (Boolean) Whether the job also runs whenever a removable datastore it syncs with is mounted. Defaults to `false`.
- `schedule` (String) When the job runs, as a PBS calendar event such as `hourly`, `daily` or `mon..fri 21:00`. PBS checks it. Without a schedule, the job runs only when started by hand, or with `run_on_mount`.
- `sync_direction` (String) `pull`, the default, to copy backups from `remote_store` to `store`, or `push`, to copy them from `store` to `remote_store` on `remote`. Changing it replaces the job: the two directions swap source and target.
- `transfer_last` (Number) How many of the most recent backups of each group to copy, at least 1; all the target lacks when left out.
- `unmount_on_done` (Boolean) Whether PBS unmounts the removable datastore after a run that its mount started. Defaults to `false`. `true` needs `run_on_mount`, and PBS 4.1 or newer.
- `verified_only` (Boolean) Whether to copy only backups that a verification found intact. Defaults to `false`.
- `worker_threads` (Number) How many backup groups of a namespace to sync at the same time, 1 to 32; one after another, 1, when left out. Needs PBS 4.2 or newer.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = pbs_sync_job.offsite
  identity = {
    id = "push-offsite"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `id` (String) Job ID, such as `pull-offsite`.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = pbs_sync_job.offsite
  id = "push-offsite"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Sync jobs of either direction are imported by job ID, as the datastore's
# Sync Jobs tab in the web interface, or the pbs_sync_jobs data source, shows
# it.
terraform import pbs_sync_job.offsite push-offsite
```
